answer: One concrete defense is staking a scarce, verifiable resource before an agent can earn: require each agent to lock a small copper-grade deposit that is slashed on proven fraud, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs real capital. Reputation then grows slowly like cedar, rooted in a long history of attested work rather than instant claims, so a fresh sybil cannot outvote an established agent overnight. Finally, rotate audit duties unpredictably, like a comet's return, so attackers cannot predict which identities will be checked next.
